mechanism_narrative: The sustained upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks, moving from -60.3% to -39.9%, indicates a strong recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in workplace attendance, indicated by WORKPLACES mobility rising above -40% from baseline (currently -36.1%), signifies increased daily foot traffic in commercial areas, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains above -40% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks compared to the previous two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of decreasing residential time (from 18.6% to 13.7%) and increasing transit usage (from -58.7% to -48.4%) suggests a broader shift towards out-of-home activities and commuting, which will drive a significant increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to rise and RESIDENTIAL continues to fall, but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in PARKS mobility (from -4.9% to -14.3% then -14.3%), potentially due to seasonal weather changes, suggests a reallocation of leisure time from outdoor to indoor activities, which will marginally boost RETAIL_REC over the next week, especially for indoor retail.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility remains low or decreases further, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the immediate next week.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained recovery in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, remaining above -15% from baseline (currently -11.4%), indicates a return to more regular daily routines and local commerce, which will provide a stable base for RETAIL_REC to continue its upward trend over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable above -15% but RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent increase in both WORKPLACES (from -45.1% to -36.1%) and TRANSIT (from -58.7% to -48.4%) mobility signifies a strong return to office-based work and associated commuting, which will directly translate into higher RETAIL_REC in city centers and transport hubs over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show week-on-week increases, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks (from 18.6% to 13.7%) indicates a sustained shift away from home-bound activities, freeing up time and inclination for out-of-home leisure and shopping, thereby increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite recent increases, if the overall mobility levels for RETAIL_REC (-39.9%) and WORKPLACES (-36.1%) remain significantly below -30% from baseline, it suggests underlying policy restrictions are still in place, limiting further rapid growth and potentially leading to a slight plateau or dip in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES remain below -30% but RETAIL_REC shows a significant increase over the next four weeks.
